short.en: The machine turns round, so must the circuit

t.en: So far the machine has always started in the top-left corner and worked row by row. Why can’t it just start anywhere?
Because each cell reads the cells above it and to its left. If those are still empty, the machine can’t go on.
This level’s robot has been fitted backwards: it can only start from the bottom-right corner and walk the rows in reverse. The small number in each cell’s corner is the order in which it gets there.

The Route Counter reads up and left, but on this machine those cells are always still empty. Think of it differently: could the number in each cell mean something else? In the end, the answer has to appear on the start.

goal.en: Routes still only go right or down, but the robot walks backwards from the bottom-right corner. Build a board so that the start cell in the top-left corner ends up with the number of routes from start to end.

how.en: The This cell panel adds “is end”. If the robot reads a cell that is still empty, it stops.

title.en: The order decides what can be read

body.en: The machine works from the bottom right to the top left, so whenever a cell is computed, the cells to its right and below are already done. That is why the circuit can only read those two directions.
The order and the circuit go together: compute the cells that others depend on before the cells that depend on them. Programmers call an order like that a “topological order”.
The start cell’s answer is the same as before. Counting from the start to the end and counting back from the end to the start are two ways of asking the same question.

note.en: A valid order: every cell comes after the cells it reads.

say.en: The robot walks from the bottom right to the top left, so when it reaches a cell, the cells above and to its left are still empty and can’t be read.
Counting from here to the end means counting back from the end. The 1 belongs on the end, not on the start.

hints.en: On this machine, only right and down can be read. Leaving this cell, where can the first step go?
From the end to the end counts as 1 route: let a 1 through on “is end”.
The Route Counter works too: right into “up”, down into “left”, and is end into “start”.
